messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: paging delivery failed for routing key `prod-primary`. 3 failed attempts, last error `http 504` from pagerflow API. automatic retry scheduled in 30s
pagerflow-bot: queued -> sending -> failed (504) for request id 1a2b3c. response body: `Gateway Timeout`
maya: saw the alert, jumping in. are customers impacted or just paging?
kevin: looks like only paging to phone/SMS. notifications in Slack channel still posted. no user-facing incidents reported yet.
jorge: paging gateway (pagerflow) has been flapping since 02:12 UTC. logs show increased latency to upstream notify service. possible downstream timeout config change?
lia: can someone confirm if dedicated fallback (email/escalation) kicked in?
sarah: escalation policy shows last step is paging -> slack -> email. slack notifications happened, so escalation path continued but phone pages didn't go out.
maya: okay, so customer-facing alerting still visible in console but oncall wasn't paged. big risk if primary oncall is offline.
kevin: i'm temporarily switching primary policy to use alternate routing key (prod-secondary) to force pages through an independent path. doing manual step now: `/pagerduty override --policy prod-primary --route prod-secondary`
kevin: done. sending a test page to myself: `curl -X POST https://pagerflow.local/send -d '{"key":"prod-secondary","message":"test page from kevin"}'`
kevin: test page delivered. :thumbsup:
maya: thanks. how did the queue get into this state? any automation that retries then drops after TTL?
jorge: digging into pagerflow logs. there's a backlog tracker that drops messages after 120s TTL if upstream doesn't ack. seeing a spike in 504s and then a flood of TTL drops.
pagerflow-bot: INFO: backlog size 0 -> 120 -> 0 within 3m. 172 messages dropped due to TTL. sample dropped id: 4f6e7d
lia: that's a lot. do we have any customers who rely on phone pages for high-sev? might need to manually escalate if they were missed.
sarah: i'm compiling a quick list from the last hour of incidents with severity >= P2. share in a sec.
maya: also, the incident runbook (paging fallback) expects automatic re-route to `prod-secondary` after 3 failed attempts. seems the failover automation didn't trigger. could be an orchestration bug.
kevin: hypothesizing: pagerflow returned 504 which the automation treated as transient but the circuit opened before re-route step executed. need to check the state machine.
jorge: found a recent deploy in eng-infra earlier today that bumped http client timeout from 10s -> 5s to reduce resource usage. that would increase 504s upstream. reverting now.
jorge: rolling back deploy `infra/pagerflow-client@deploy-2026-03-12-09` to previous version. ETA ~3m.
maya: while that's rolling, we should backfill missed pages: run manual escalation to secondaries and email primary oncall list. who has permissions?
kevin: I do. I'll run manual escalate for the window 02:10 -> 02:40 UTC. command: `/pagerduty escalate --window 02:10-02:40 --policy prod-primary --method phone,email`
kevin: done. confirmations show calls placed to secondary number pool.
sarah: sent a note to customer success to proactively reach out to customers with critical integrations. cc @lia
lia: thanks — i'll assist with account lookup. please drop incident ids for the timeframe once you have them.
pagerflow-bot: ROLLBACK complete for `infra/pagerflow-client@deploy-2026-03-12-09`. health check passed. 200 OK to upstream notify service.
jorge: after rollback, upstream latency returned to normal, backlog cleared. monitoring alert cleared at 02:28 UTC.
maya: fab. follow-ups: 1) add a canary check to detect client timeout regresses; 2) ensure failover automation triggers on 504 semantics, not only 5xx/connection error; 3) add metric for TTL-dropped pages and alert when > 10 in 5m.
kevin: i'll own the automation semantics change (2). adding a unit + integration test to simulate 504 behavior.
jorge: i'll add the canary and metric (1 + 3).
sarah: i'll own customer comms and postmortem note. quick ask: do we want to change the runbook to instruct manual override earliest after first missed page rather than waiting for 3 attempts?
maya: let's leave runbook but add explicit 'if pages to phone fail, immediately check alternate route' — minor wording tweak.
lia: pinging legal for any regulated account notifications.
kevin: creating an incident ticket with summary: `Pagerflow client timeout change caused TTL drops of phone pages; failover automation did not trigger for 504`. attaching logs and timeline. ticket id INC-2026-5123
maya: great. please add the mitigation steps and owners we discussed.
sarah: postmortem assigned. we'll schedule a blameless review tomorrow 15:00 UTC. :calendar:
